Topic.label: Combined Problems on Inverse Proportion Functions and Linear Functions

Question: The graphs of the linear function \(y=x-1\) and the inverse proportional function \(y=6/x\) intersect at points \(A\) and \(B\), with \(A\) in the first quadrant. The line \(y=x-1\) intersects the \(y\)-axis at \(C\). Find the area of \(\triangle AOB\). (You may write your answer as a fraction.)
Solution: Combining the equations gives \(x^2-x-6=0\), so \(x=3\) or \(-2\), giving \(A(3,2)\) and \(B(-2,-3)\). Also, \(C(0,-1)\) and \(OC=1\). Thus, \(S_{\triangle AOB}=S_{\triangle AOC}+S_{\triangle BOC}=(1/2)\times1\times3+(1/2)\times1\times2=5/2\).
